column4: SIGSEGV after ~11 output blocks of zeroth-order creation (NULL -> A(ser)) from A:0. Master and the result-preserving build fail at the same point; the full branch fails later on the same fault.

No bimolecular association reaction, so set_rMaxLimit() leaves rMaxLimit at 0 and SimulVolume::Dimensions divides the box length by it. Cell count goes negative and the run prints "CELL PAIR MAX EXCEEDED / Current number of cells: -4" indefinitely (~110M messages in 30 s) without advancing. Identical on all three builds.

SIGSEGV immediately after "BEGIN SIMULATION", seed-dependent: it crashes on master and on the result-preserving build with seed 20260810 but completes on both with seeds 1-5. A latent memory error, not a systematic failure. The full branch happens to survive seed 20260810 because its initial orientations differ; that is luck, not a fix.
Runs correctly, but the model holds a single molecule (A:1) so no reaction path is exercised. Excluded as a benchmark, not as a failure.

SIGSEGV between 8000 and 12000 iterations: completes at 4000 and 8000, faults at 12000, 16000 and 20000. Reproduces identically on the pre-refactor binary (nerdss-optimized at 207e22d), so it is the model or a latent memory error, not the consolidation work. The case is still useful below the threshold and is in coverage_cases.tsv at nItr 4000, because it is the only sample that reaches check_compartment_reaction and the compartment transmission probabilities.
